definitions.explanation: A Japanese herb (Cryptotaenia japonica) with three-lobed leaves and a mild, celery-like flavor. Widely used as a garnish and aromatic in Japanese cuisine.

examples.japanese: {茶碗蒸|ちゃわんむ}しに{三|み}つ{葉|ば}をのせる。
examples.english: To place mitsuba on top of chawanmushi.

examples.japanese: お{吸|す}い{物|もの}の{仕上|しあ}げに{三|み}つ{葉|ば}を{添|そ}えた。
examples.english: I added mitsuba as a finishing touch to the clear soup.

examples.japanese: {三|み}つ{葉|ば}は{香|かお}りが{良|よ}いので、{和食|わしょく}の{彩|いろど}りや{風味|ふうみ}{付|づ}けによく{使|つか}われる。
examples.english: Mitsuba has a pleasant aroma, so it is often used to add color and flavor to Japanese dishes.

notes:
WRITING:
The name literally means "three leaves" ({三|み}つ{葉|ば}), referring to its distinctive three-lobed leaf structure.

CULTURE:
Mitsuba is a staple herb in Japanese cooking, used similarly to how parsley or cilantro is used in Western cuisine. It is commonly added to {茶碗蒸|ちゃわんむ}し (savory egg custard), {親子丼|おやこどん} (chicken and egg rice bowl), and clear soups. It wilts quickly when heated, so it is typically added at the very end of cooking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三|み}つ{葉|ば}を{添|そ}える: to garnish with mitsuba
- {三|み}つ{葉|ば}の{香|かお}り: the aroma of mitsuba
